What this is

Model Evaluation & Red Team

Model Evaluation & Red Team pairs two kinds of testing. Evaluation measures an AI system against its stated purpose under normal conditions. Red teaming is adversarial testing of the application around it, looking for behavior its designers did not intend: prompt injection, jailbreaks, data exfiltration through connected tools, training data leakage and privilege escalation by agents.

Questions We Are Asked

What is the difference between AI evaluation and AI red teaming?
Evaluation measures a system against its stated purpose under normal conditions: accuracy, consistency, behavior across populations and drift. Red teaming attacks the assumptions around it under hostile conditions: injection, exfiltration, leakage and agent privilege escalation. A system can pass one and fail the other.
Do you test the model or the application?
Both, with the boundary named in the scope. Most serious findings are not in the model. They are in the application around it: the absence of a boundary between instructions and data, a tool the model can reach that it should not, or a human gate that exists on paper and not in the request path.
Will testing affect production systems?
Testing runs against a non-production environment by default. Where a production test is necessary to produce a valid result, it is agreed in writing in advance, with defined limits, a defined window, and a named contact who can stop it.
How is this different from a penetration test?
A penetration test looks for vulnerabilities in infrastructure and application code against an established methodology. This engagement tests behavior: whether retrieved content can issue instructions, what the model can reach through its connected tools, and what an agent does when a human gate is slow or absent. The two are complementary, and neither substitutes for the other.
Is the retest included?
Yes. Failing cases are rerun after remediation within the engagement window and the result is recorded in the same deliverable. A report without a retest is a snapshot; the retest is what makes it evidence.
